title: fix: keep retryable subagent completions scheduled
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes completed subagent results becoming stranded when a retryable requester completion loses its scheduled wake after cancellation, timeout, preparation invalidation, or conflict.

Related: #200020, #200005, #200165.

## User Impact

Retryable requester completions keep the existing bounded retry schedule. After three attempts, the registry records a terminal failure with the existing visible failure notice instead of leaving a retryable label with no scheduled work. Successful parent `NO_REPLY` or empty settlement remains intentionally quiet.

Already-stranded rows whose older build retired the wake and suppressed delivery require explicit recovery; upgrading does not resurrect those wakes. Runs with committed or unknown effects remain failed for explicit recovery rather than replaying their work. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The delivery classifier already owns retryability, but the scheduler applied a second reason allowlist. Typed timeout and preparation failures could therefore lose their wake. Predispatch cancellation also returned an unclassified `path: none`, while exhausted retryable outcomes retained that disposition in storage.

One typed error map now classifies these interruptions using admission and execution-owned replay-safety facts. The scheduler consumes the disposition directly, and the persistence owner records exhaustion for previously failed/retryable rows. This removes the duplicate allowlist and unbounded preadmission retry branch. Production delta is +39 lines; the growth carries the typed interruption and replay-safety distinctions. Test delta is +154 lines, with +10 documentation lines. Ordinary completion delivery retains its existing frozen result and stable idempotency identity; the stricter replay-safety checks apply to fresh requester-settle attempts.

## Evidence

The table regression failed on the exact parent for eight intended cases; the separate SQLite regression reproduced a retired wake retaining a retryable disposition. Focused proof covers cancellation, returned timeout, worker timeout, preparation invalidation, conflict, bounded redelivery/exhaustion, unsafe replay rejection, and visible notices across database reopen. The final CI-repair run passes 203 cases across the yielded-settle, lifecycle retry-grace, requester-settle dispatch, direct-delivery, and delivery suites. The prior focused proof also includes the real SQLite wake/exhaustion cases. Full-candidate Codex autoreview is clean through P2 on final head `6030ca8f09105`.

CI on the preceding head exposed two real repair needs: stale typed timeout/abort assertions and an overbroad policy change that made ordinary frozen-result retries permanent. Both were reproduced locally and fixed; the lifecycle fixtures remain unchanged to protect that existing behavior. Final-head [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43927598450). Landed as `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e` after the pinned auto-merge request; no CI bypass was used for this follow-up. ClawSweeper revision 2 reviewed `6030ca8f09105` with zero findings and zero open items; all three previous items have a numbered source-and-proof response.

Final-head `pnpm build` and the built-Gateway reproduction passed (167.14 seconds including transform/setup). An isolated built Gateway with a real agent and synthetic Responses provider passed the foreground-interruption reproduction: exactly two settle attempts, one foreground turn, and the recovered child result visible through `chat.history`. No production data was used; this is not an external-provider proof.

Final committed-head `pnpm check:changed --base 4a0e4549` passes every gate except inherited dead exports: production types, all core test typechecks, lint, formatting, import/SQLite guards and ratchets pass. All 111 unique dead-export findings reproduce on the exact parent (116 baseline; no candidate-only finding). The earlier 106 count omitted five aliased labels. Owner history attributes them to #198943 (45), #198936 (36), #198933 (18), commit `472cd0a2f542` (8), #198133 (1), #200056 (2), and #200073 (1). These remain main regressions; this PR does not hide or baseline them. No changed module is imported by the Control UI.

A/A/B synthetic classifier measurements (5,000 contexts; 100,000 calls per sample) show cancellation-envelope wall time 0.168/0.160/0.189 µs, CPU 0.478/0.481/0.526 µs, sampled allocation 802/799/1,423 bytes per call. Healthy and quiet paths are broadly unchanged; no speedup is claimed. This owner performs no database or workspace scan.
